statement.p: Sketch the region of integration and evaluate by changing to polar coordinates:

static.solution:
9\le x\le 18,\quad 0\le y\le \sqrt{18 x-x^2} For f(x)=\sqrt{18 x-x^2}, and R=9
We first describe \mathcal{D} in polar coordinates. The region lies in the angular sector 0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4}.
The circle y=\sqrt{18 x-x^2} or {( x-9 )}^2+{y}^2=81, y\ge 0 (obtained by completing the square)
is the circle of radius 9 and center ( 9,0 ).
Its polar equation is r=18 \cos \theta. The polar equation of the line x=9 is r \cos \theta =9 or r=9 \sec \theta.
R=9 , and \quad 9 \sec \theta \le r \le 18 \cos \theta
Therefore, \mathcal{D} has the following description: 0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4},\quad 9 \sec \theta \le r\le 18 \cos \theta Using change of variables we get \begin{array}{rcl} \int_{9}^{18} \int_0^{\sqrt{18 x-x^2}} \frac{dy \,dx}{\sqrt{{x}^2+{y}^2}}\amp =\amp \int_0^{\pi/4}\int_{9\sec\theta}^{18\cos\theta}\frac1{r}\cdot r\,dr\,d\theta\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^{\pi/4}\int_{9\sec\theta}^{18\cos\theta}\,dr\,d\theta\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^{\pi/4} r\bigg|_{r=9\sec\theta}^{18\cos\theta} \,d\theta\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^{\pi/4} ( 18 \cos \theta -9 \sec \theta ) \,d\theta\\ \amp =\amp 18\sin \theta \bigg|_0^{\pi/4}- 9\ln ( \sec \theta + \tan \theta)\bigg|_0^{\pi/4}\\ \amp =\amp 9\left(2 \sin \frac{\pi }{4}-\left( \ln \left( \sec \frac{\pi }{4}+ \tan \frac{\pi }{4}\right)- \ln 1\right)\right)\\ \amp =\amp 9\left(2\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}- \ln \left(\sqrt{2}+1\right)\right)\\ \amp =\amp 9\left(\sqrt{2}- \ln \left(1+\sqrt{2}\right)\right)\\ \amp \approx\amp 4.79556 \end{array}
